title: Rosalind and the Debt
premise: Ulyana Voss, a veteran interpreter for a faltering peace delegation, discovers that her own voiceprint—harvested years ago during a translation session—unlocks a hidden server containing plans for a staged 'accident' designed to collapse the negotiations and reignite a war. The server was triggered by her estranged brother Tomas, who inherited their father's intelligence archives and has been hunted ever since for trying to expose them. As Ulyana races across two continents to find Tomas and stop the attack, she must decide whether loyalty to her delegation's handlers or the truth buried in her family's past matters more. In the end, she broadcasts the archive herself at the moment of the attack, sacrificing her career and nearly her life, exposing the conspirators and forcing the peace process to survive on honest terms.
about_author: Wren Fairweather is the pen name of a former diplomatic translator turned novelist who spent a decade working behind closed doors in Geneva and Vienna. Their fiction explores what people owe to institutions—and what institutions owe to the truth.

chapters.title: The Language of Failure
chapters.summary: Ulyana interprets a doomed opening session of the peace talks, sensing that both delegations are performing rather than negotiating. Her POV establishes her weary professionalism and the delegation's quiet rot. Emotional beat: disillusionment masked as duty.

chapters.title: A Voiceprint in the Dark
chapters.summary: At 3 a.m., an automated call plays her own recorded voice back to her, then unlocks a remote server's welcome screen before cutting off. POV: Ulyana. She recognizes the voice sample from a session six years ago. Emotional beat: cold dread—the past has been listening.

chapters.title: What Father Left
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Ulyana's POV: her father's death, his sealed footlockers, and her brother Tomas's obsession with them. She remembers refusing to help him open them. Emotional beat: guilt over the family fracture she helped cause.

chapters.title: The Delegation's Quiet Man
chapters.summary: Delegation security officer Brandt begins asking Ulyana oddly specific questions about her family history. POV alternates between Ulyana and Brandt, who knows more than he says. Emotional beat: paranoia blooming inside institutional trust.

chapters.title: Server on Another Continent
chapters.summary: Ulyana traces the server's location to a data center outside Tallinn using fragments of the unlock message. POV: Ulyana, with a tense interlude from Tomas hiding in Riga. Emotional beat: the pull of inheritance—she boards a plane against orders.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: In Tallinn, a retired archivist explains how her father's generation built deniable systems whose rules were rewritten after every war. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: understanding that her whole career served machinery, not peace.

chapters.title: The Accident Schedule
chapters.summary: Inside the server, Ulyana finds a timeline: an 'infrastructure failure' timed to coincide with the summit's final week, engineered to look like sabotage by one side. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: horror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Brother, Where Are You
chapters.summary: Tomas contacts her through a dead-drop protocol their father taught them as children. POV shifts to Tomas: hunted, exhausted, certain their father's archive can stop the plot. Emotional beat: wary hope between siblings.

chapters.title: Brandt's Offer
chapters.summary: Brandt confronts Ulyana with evidence she's been flagged, offering protection if she surrenders what she found. POV: Ulyana. She realizes he may be part of the conspiracy—or its last honest man. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made personal.

chapters.title: Riga Rain
chapters.summary: Ulyana slips her minders and reaches Tomas in Riga; their reunion is all accusation and unfinished grief until they open the footlocker together. POV: alternating siblings. Emotional beat: catharsis—twenty years of silence breaking.

chapters.title: The Archive of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: The father's documents reveal the attack's architects: a cabal within both delegations' security services profiting from perpetual negotiation. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: bitter clarity—the enemy wears familiar badges.

chapters.title: Someone Is Following the Rules
chapters.summary: A tail from the delegation catches up; a chase through Riga's old town ends with Tomas wounded and the archive drive nearly lost. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: fear fusing into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Back at the summit, Ulyana must translate a speech she now knows is cover for the plot, rendering lies faithfully while deciding whether to break. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the cost of professional neutrality.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: She passes a copy of the archive to a sympathetic journalist via the old family protocol, knowing it will burn her. POV: journalist Ilse, briefly, then Ulyana. Emotional beat: crossing the point of no return.

chapters.title: Countdown at the Substation
chapters.summary: The siblings identify the target: a power substation whose 'failure' will black out the signing ceremony and be blamed on the other side. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: urgency compressing everything.

chapters.title: Trusted Hands
chapters.summary: Ulyana tests Brandt by feeding him false details; his reaction exposes him as complicit—or brilliantly loyal. A second test settles it: he reports to the cabal. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed, grief deferred.

chapters.title: Locked Rooms
chapters.summary: Detained in the delegation compound, Ulyana escapes using an interpreter's knowledge of the building's bilingual signage and service routes. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: competence as rebellion.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Tomas and Ulyana prepare the broadcast plan: hijack the summit's closed-circuit feed with the archive at the exact hour of the staged attack. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: quiet courage before the storm.

chapters.title: Accident, Scheduled
chapters.summary: The attack begins—a fire in the substation, alarms rising—as Ulyana fights through locked corridors to reach the broadcast room. POV: Ulyana, kinetic and breathless. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into momentum.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: Ulyana uses her own harvested voiceprint—the very thing that started it—to authenticate the archive live, exposing the cabal mid-attack as delegates watch. Brandt tries to stop her; Tomas intervenes. Emotional beat: truth spoken in her own voice, finally.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: The attack fails to stick; arrests ripple through both delegations, and the talks resume under scrutiny rather than theater. Ulyana faces inquiry, stripped of clearance but vindicated. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: exhaustion and fragile justice.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Debt
chapters.summary: Epilogue: months later, Ulyana and Tomas visit their father's grave, having learned why he built the archive—he meant it as a debt owed to the future, not a weapon. She takes honest work teaching interpreters. Emotional beat: reconciliation with memory, and peace chosen over loyalty to lies.
